 Stephen Curry tallied 25 points (6-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Curry only played 21 minutes in Monday’s blowout victory, none in the fourth quarter. That’s all the time he needed to notch another career milestone, as the Warriors guard moved past DeMar DeRozan into 16th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list. Thus far, Curry’s production has exceeded his preseason ADP by a safe distance, as he’s been a top-5 player in nine-cat formats. The Warriors end their week with games against the Rockets and Spurs, two teams that should offer up greater resistance than the Pelicans did.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday. 
 Curry’s sublime start to the year continued in this one as he topped the 40-point plateau for the second time in eight games. His signature sequence came in the final minute of regulation when he knocked down a three-pointer before sinking a pair of free throws and converting a go-ahead layup in the closing seconds. He added five points in overtime as Golden State was finally able to pull away for good. The 38-year-old legend has delivered first-round fantasy value so far, averaging 31.3 points through eight games. Are you not entertained? The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday. 
 Despite a rough start to this game, Curry got going in the third quarter. After scoring seven points on 2-of-10 shooting in the first half, he scored 14 points in the third quarter alone and eight more points in the fourth to steal the win for Golden State. Curry has been unbelievable to start the season, which has him ranked as one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point. He’ll look to stay hot against the Magic to wrap up the week on Saturday.

 Stephen Curry tallied 34 points (9-of-21 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 While he didn’t have his best night shooting the basketball, Curry extended his streak of games with at least 31 points to three. The Warriors star was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 6-of-9 from the field and scoring 18 points. Outside that period, the Suns kept Curry in check, but he still went home with a stat line that many fantasy managers will take without hesitation.

 Curry is going to sit out Sunday for right knee injury management reasons. Will Richard is likely the top candidate to move into the starting lineup with Curry sidelined.

 #30 
 Stephen Curry finished Friday’s win over the Lakers with 31 points (11-of-23 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and eight three-pointers. 
 The Warriors got off to a terribly slow start, being outscored 38-15 in the first quarter. The bench came up big in the second quarter, setting the stage for Curry to do his usual work in the second half. He scored 17 of his 31 after halftime, helping the Warriors turn a 25-point deficit into a 17-point victory. During the fourth quarter, Curry moved into 18th on the NBA’s all-time scoring list, passing Dominique Wilkins. Over the last two games, he’s scored 75 points and knocked down 14 three-pointers.

 Stephen Curry with an absolute monster performance with 44 points (11-of-27 FGs, 16-of-16 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, two steals, and six 3-pointers in 119-114 win against the Timberwolves. 
 Steph can still go crazy in games but it doesn’t happen as often with his age. Getting a perfect 16-16 from the free throw line is an incredible boost to your fantasy teams at this point in the week. As long as he is healthy, he will be one of the most exciting players in the NBA, and you can take any of these performances you can get as a fantasy owner.

 Stephen Curry accounted for 24 points (8-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets. 
 For just the second time in his illustrious career, Curry finished a game without missing a shot. After making his lone attempt during the first half, the Warriors guard shot 7-of-7 from the field in the second half as they pulled away from the Nuggets. Given Yaxel Lendeborg’s play, the Warriors didn’t have to rely as much on Curry. If that continues, it would make the future Hall of Fame guard’s job a little easier.

 Stephen Curry tallied 24 points (5-of-15 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Curry led the Warriors in scoring on Friday, but he shot a frigid 5-of-15 from the field. The assists were solid, but this was not the best night to have the Warriors star in most fantasy lineups. After the game, Curry said he “probably” won’t play against the Suns on Saturday, bad news for fantasy managers hoping for a bounce-back effort.

 Derik Queen notched 16 points (4-of-8 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds and three blocks in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Queen did most of his damage offensively in the second quarter, scoring eight of his 16 points. However, of greater importance to fantasy managers may be the three blocks, a new season-high and two shy of the second-year forward/center’s career high. However, his defense remains a work in progress, even with the blocks recorded on Monday. While Queen has been a consistently productive option for fantasy managers, the defensive issues are why he’s averaging 22 minutes per game and not more.

 Jeremiah Fears accounted for 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Fears led the Pelicans with eight assists, but he also recorded six turnovers in Monday’s 138-87 defeat. This was one of his poorer performances of the season, and the Pelicans not having Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson didn’t help either. Fears will look to bounce back on Wednesday when the Pelicans host the Nets. That should be a better matchup for him than the red-hot Warriors were.

 Dejounte Murray tallied 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 The Pelicans didn’t have Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson on Monday, and those absences were certainly felt. Murray shot a solid percentage from the field and led the Pelicans starters in scoring, but it wasn’t enough when the Warriors knocked down 21 three-pointers. Murray has been close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats, but it’s fair to wonder if his presence in the lineup has limited Jeremiah Fears’ fantasy ceiling. That’s something to watch as the season progresses.

 Melton was one of four Warriors to make at least four three-pointers in Monday’s blowout victory.  Yaxel Lendeborg produced 23 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Lendeborg continues to shine for the Warriors, making all four of his three-point attempts on Monday. The rookie forward has scored at least 20 points in six of 11 games and is considered by many to be one of the early favorites for Rookie of the Year. The Warriors play two more games this week, at Houston and San Antonio, so we’ll learn a bit more about Lendeborg in games of that magnitude.

 Podziemski shot 5-of-11 from beyond the arc on Monday, a season high for three-pointers in a game for the fourth-year guard. Even better for fantasy managers, Podz recorded a complete stat line, his third in as many games. Based on his ADP, Podziemski wasn’t expected to be a top-100 player this season.
